_about: Narration for the Storyraise Donor Signals walkthrough. `text` is what viewers read in captions; [[cue:name]] markers are stripped before TTS and become timestamps visuals land on. `respell` maps a caption word to how the voice should say it (applied to the TTS text only). This is an overview, not a reading of the screen: the page's own sentences stay on the page. Labels match the product UI. American English, no em dashes.

scenes.title: Cold open
scenes.text: Your donor database knows who gave. [[cue:question]]It cannot tell you who is about to stop. [[cue:brand]]Donor Signals scores every donor you have, overnight, and tells you who to call first.

scenes.title: How the year is going
scenes.text: [[cue:strip]]It starts where your board starts. [[cue:retention]]Did last year's donors come back, [[cue:fytd]]is the money ahead or behind, [[cue:firstyear]]and did the new ones stay. Each one carries what it should be measured against, so you can tell a good year from a lucky one.

scenes.title: Six groups
scenes.text: [[cue:tiles]]Under that, your whole file sorted by what each donor needs next. [[cue:money]]With the money at stake on every group, so you can see where an hour of your week is worth the most.

scenes.title: At risk, their own rhythm
scenes.text: [[cue:atrisk]]At risk is where most tools get it wrong. [[cue:cadence]]They pick a number of days and call everyone past it lapsed. Storyraise measures each donor against their own rhythm. A monthly donor who has missed three gifts is late. An annual donor who gave in November is not. [[cue:sorted]]And the list leads with the most at stake.

scenes.title: Why now
scenes.text: [[cue:row]]Every donor comes with the reason they are in front of you, [[cue:reason]]in a sentence, not a score you have to decode. [[cue:reads]]And because Storyraise publishes your reports, it knows something your database does not: [[cue:moat]]who is still reading you after they stopped giving. Those are the ones you can win back.

scenes.title: Read it or compare it
scenes.text: [[cue:views]]Overview reads as a list of people. [[cue:table]]Table puts the same donors in a grid you can sort. Whichever you use is remembered.

scenes.title: Make something
scenes.text: [[cue:actions]]Then the part that makes this worth your morning. [[cue:cards]]Every group comes with two things you can make for it, already written for that moment. Record one video for everyone who just gave, [[cue:report]]or build a report that shows them what their money did.

scenes.title: Three routes
scenes.text: [[cue:dialog]]Open one and half the work is done. [[cue:routes]]Start from a draft written for this group, a template, or a report you have already published. [[cue:carry]]The group comes with you, and each donor gets a page with their own name on it.

scenes.title: Giving health
scenes.text: [[cue:health]]And once a month, the longer view. [[cue:bands]]Retention by gift size is the one that changes plans. Your smallest donors come back about a third of the time. Donors giving in the thousands come back nearly nine times in ten. That is where next year's plan comes from.

scenes.title: Explore
scenes.text: [[cue:cta]]All of this comes out of the donor data you already have. Give it one morning, and find out who has been waiting to hear from you.
